Hot config reload for long-running yolo-agent watchers
description: Long-running watchers should pick up .yolo-runner/config.yaml edits without a restart. Today tracker-watch resolves trackerAgentConfig once at startup (cmd/yolo-agent/tracker_watch.go:38) and threads that stale value through every poll iteration, and both tracker-watch and arc-review-watch capture poll_interval at startup. arc-review-watch already re-resolves its config every iteration (arc_review_watch.go:114) but nothing pins that behavior. This epic makes per-iteration config resolution the rule: labels, status transitions, agent defaults, and poll intervals apply on the next poll after a config edit. Deliberately startup-bound and out of scope: lock_path (the held lock is never re-acquired), state_path, events path/stream wiring, and profile/tracker endpoint identity.

title: HCR-01 Resolve tracker agent config per tracker-watch iteration
description:
Why: Label, status-transition, and tracker-agent setting edits currently require restarting tracker-watch because the config is resolved once at startup and captured in the poll closure.

In scope:
- Move ResolveTrackerAgentConfig from defaultRunTrackerWatch into runTrackerWatchPollIteration so each iteration uses a freshly resolved trackerAgentConfig.
- Keep lock acquisition on the startup-resolved lock_path; a lock_path edit mid-run is ignored until restart.

Out of scope:
- No poll interval changes.
- No agent defaults/profile reload changes.
- No re-locking.

Strict TDD:
1. Add a failing test with a fake config service returning different label sets per call; assert the second iteration uses the second label set.
2. Confirm it fails (config captured at startup).
3. Move resolution inside the iteration minimally.
4. Re-run the targeted test.
5. Run go test ./cmd/yolo-agent -run TrackerWatch.

Done when:
- A config edit between iterations changes the labels used by the next iteration in the test.

Expected files:
- cmd/yolo-agent/tracker_watch.go
- cmd/yolo-agent/tracker_watch_test.go

Depends on: none
Unlocks: HCR-03

title: HCR-02 Accept an interval provider in the shared poll loop
description:
Why: Both watch loops take a fixed time.Duration, so poll_interval edits never apply; the loop needs to ask for the interval before each wait.

In scope:
- Change runTrackerWatchPollLoop (and its arc-review wrapper if separate) to take a func() time.Duration interval provider, calling it before each wait.
- Update existing call sites mechanically with a constant provider so behavior is unchanged.

Out of scope:
- No dynamic providers at call sites yet.
- No new validation of interval values beyond what exists.

Strict TDD:
1. Add a failing poll-loop unit test with a provider returning increasing values; assert each wait receives the fresh value.
2. Confirm it fails (signature takes a fixed duration).
3. Change the signature and loop body minimally; fix call sites with constant providers.
4. Re-run the targeted test.
5. Run go test ./cmd/yolo-agent -run PollLoop.

Done when:
- The loop queries the provider before every wait in the test and existing loop tests still pass.

Expected files:
- cmd/yolo-agent/tracker_watch.go
- cmd/yolo-agent/tracker_watch_test.go

Depends on: none
Unlocks: HCR-03, HCR-04

title: HCR-03 Wire dynamic poll interval in tracker-watch
description:
Why: With per-iteration config resolution and a provider-based loop, tracker-watch can honor poll_interval edits on the next wait.

In scope:

Out of scope:
- No arc-review-watch changes.
- No mid-wait interruption when the interval shrinks; the new value applies to the next wait.

Strict TDD:

2. Confirm it fails (constant provider).
3. Wire the dynamic provider minimally.
4. Re-run the targeted test.

Done when:

title: HCR-05 Pin per-iteration config reload in arc-review-watch with a regression test
description:
Why: arc-review-watch resolving its config every iteration is the behavior the allow_ship rollout flow relies on, and no test currently fails if someone hoists the resolution out of the loop.

In scope:
- Add a regression test: fake config service flips allow_ship (or another per-iteration field like max_concurrency) between two iterations; assert the second iteration observes the new value.

Out of scope:
- No production changes (test-only; if the test reveals startup capture, stop and record findings).

Strict TDD:
1. Write the test asserting the second iteration sees the flipped value.
2. Run it; it should pass against current per-iteration resolution. Temporarily hoist resolution locally to confirm the test catches the regression, then revert the hoist.
3. Keep the passing test.
4. Re-run the targeted test.
5. Run go test ./cmd/yolo-agent -run ArcReviewWatch.

Done when:
- The regression test exists, passes, and demonstrably fails when resolution is hoisted to startup.

- cmd/yolo-agent/arc_review_watch_test.go

title: Watcher resilience: survive transient iteration errors
description:
tracker-watch and arc-review-watch must keep monitoring their queues instead of exiting on the first failed poll iteration. Today runTrackerWatchPollLoop (cmd/yolo-agent/tracker_watch.go:109) returns on any iterate error, so one transient failure kills the whole watcher. Observed in production three times in two days: a Startrek HTTP 500 on issues/_search (adapta-watch-20260610_154329, died 03:32 after ~12h of correct operation), a stale scheduler-state 'task not found' (since fixed), and a non-idempotent status transition (since fixed). The watcher should log/emit the error, keep polling, and only exit on context cancellation or a bounded run of consecutive failures. The Startrek client should additionally retry transient 5xx responses on idempotent requests.

Sequencing note: the HCR epic (yolo-8des) also modifies runTrackerWatchPollLoop's signature (interval provider). Do not run both epics' loop tasks concurrently; land one before starting the other.

title: WRES-01 Continue polling after iteration errors in the shared poll loop
description:
Why: Any iterate error currently terminates runTrackerWatchPollLoop, so both watchers die on the first transient tracker failure.

In scope:
- Change runTrackerWatchPollLoop so an iterate error is reported via a new onIterationError callback parameter and the loop continues to the wait step.
- Exit with the last error only after a maxConsecutiveFailures run (parameter; reset the counter on any successful iteration).
- once mode keeps returning the iteration error immediately.

Out of scope:
- No call-site event emission (next tasks).
- No backoff changes; the normal poll interval is the spacing.
- No interval-provider signature work (HCR epic).

Strict TDD:
1. Add a failing loop unit test: iterate fails twice then succeeds; assert the loop keeps running, the callback saw both errors, and the counter reset; a second case asserts exit after maxConsecutiveFailures.
2. Confirm it fails (loop returns on first error).
3. Implement the minimal loop change.
4. Re-run the targeted test.
5. Run go test ./cmd/yolo-agent -run PollLoop.

Done when:
- Transient iterate errors no longer end the loop and the consecutive-failure cap is enforced in tests.

Expected files:
- cmd/yolo-agent/tracker_watch.go
- cmd/yolo-agent/tracker_watch_test.go

Depends on: none
Unlocks: WRES-02, WRES-03

title: WRES-04 Retry transient Startrek 5xx responses on idempotent requests
description:
Why: A single Startrek HTTP 500 on issues/_search killed a 12-hour watch; transient server errors on read paths should be retried before surfacing.

In scope:
- In the Startrek client request path, retry responses with status >= 500 (and connection errors) up to 3 attempts with short exponential backoff, only for idempotent requests: all GETs plus the issues/_search POST.
- Honor context cancellation between attempts.

Out of scope:
- No retries for mutating requests (transitions, comments, label PATCHes).
- No circuit breaker or metrics.

Strict TDD:
1. Add a failing client test with a fake HTTP server returning 500 twice then 200 for a search; assert success after retries; a mutating request still fails on first 500.
2. Confirm it fails (no retry today).
3. Implement the bounded retry minimally.
4. Re-run the targeted test.
5. Run go test ./internal/startrek.

Done when:
- Search survives two 500s in the test and mutations are never retried.

- internal/startrek/client.go
- internal/startrek/client_test.go

title: Arc review watch live integration: PR discovery and continuous review runner
description:
Wire yolo-agent arc-review-watch end to end so it reviews real Arcanum PRs. The ARW epic (yolo-h5wj) landed the watcher framework (sessions, SQLite state, heartbeats, stale recovery, ship gate, runbook) and the review library (internal/arcreview: prompt, result parsing, appliers, action planner) plus arc pr list parsing/filtering (internal/arcanum). Two integration points are stubs: defaultDiscoverArcReviewPRs returns nil (cmd/yolo-agent/arc_review_watch.go) and arc-pr-review-runner only supports --once heartbeat mode. This epic adds: an arc CLI exec adapter, real PR discovery over configured workspaces, PR runtime state fetch (details, comments, changed files, checks), a real Arcanum write client (inline comments, summary, reply, ship), the missing reviewed-revision store, model invocation for the review prompt, a single-cycle dispatcher, and the continuous runner loop.

Risk notes: the exact arc CLI subcommands and JSON shapes for PR details, comments, diffs, checks, posting comments, and shipping must be confirmed against arc/Arcanum on the dev host (arc pr --help, a.yandex-team.ru API docs). Any task that finds the CLI lacks the needed data must stop and record findings on the task instead of widening scope. PRSummary currently has no revision field; revision is resolved in the runtime-state fetch, not during discovery.
